sovereign_country.strategic_role: 全球跨境基金设立第一大国、超大型跨国投资架构

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Accounts Receivable Factoring and Cross-Border Reverse Factoring

applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Convention between the Grand Duchy of Luxembourg and the Kingdom of Belgium for the avoidance of double taxation (BLEU framework)
Agreement between the Belgo-Luxembourg Economic Union and the People's Republic of China for the Encouragement and Reciprocal Protection of Investments

Convention between the Grand Duchy of Luxembourg and the United States of America for the Avoidance of Double Taxation and the Prevention of Fiscal Evasion with Respect to Taxes on Income and Capital, 1996 as amended
OECD Multilateral Convention to Implement Tax Treaty Related Measures to Prevent Base Erosion and Profit Shifting

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Loi modifiée du 12 novembre 2004 relative à la lutte contre le blanchiment et le financement du terrorisme, as amended; Loi du 13 janvier 2019 instituant le Registre des bénéficiaires effectifs; Loi du 10 août 1915 concernant les sociétés commerciales, as amended; Loi du 19 décembre 2002 relative au registre de commerce et des sociétés et aux comptes annuels des entreprises, as amended; CSSF Regulation n° 12-02 of 14 December 2012, as amended; related Grand-Ducal regulations implementing EU Directive (EU) 2015/849 and Regulation (EU) 2015/847.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified copy of the passport and proof of identity of each ultimate beneficial owner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public or competent public authority in the country of origin of the UBO
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille pursuant to the Hague Convention of 5 October 1961, or consular legalization by the Luxembourg Embassy or Consulate in the document's country of origin

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Original or certified copy of the power of attorney appointing the Luxembourg authorised representative or registered office agent
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public in the UBO's or appointing entity's country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or consular legalization, with French, German, or English translation as required by the Luxembourg notary

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of incorporation, certificate of good standing, and constitutional documents of any corporate general partner or parent entity
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Home-state commercial registry or equivalent registrar
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or consular legalization, plus certified translation into Luxembourg practice language where required

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter and documented source of funds and source of wealth for each UBO and/or corporate investor
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Issuing regulated bank or financial institution in the country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarisation in origin country plus Hague Apostille or consular legalization; signature verification by the Luxembourg notary if deed remains pending

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Declaration of beneficial ownership and UBO questionnaire duly signed by the general partner and each legal entity UBO
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Luxembourg designated agent under the RBE Law
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Signed in original before a Luxembourg notary or by authenticated private document admitted by the RBE filing process

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory initial and ongoing screening of each UBO, general partner, manager, authorised signatory, beneficial owner, and relevant counterparty against the consolidated UN Security Council sanctions list, EU sanctions lists, OFAC SDN list, UK OFSI, and the national lists maintained by the Luxembourg Cellule de Renseignement Financier (CRF). PeP screening must cover family members and close associates, with enhanced due diligence applicable to any person classified as a domestic or foreign politically exposed person under the Luxembourg AML Law and Directive (EU) 2015/849. Negative screening reports must be obtained from an external compliance data provider before signing, and re-screening is required within 90 days and thereafter at least quarterly for as long as the file remains open.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) – Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) via https://www.lbr.lu online filing portal
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The name of a Société en Commandite Spéciale (SCSp) must include the phrase 'Société en commandite spéciale' or the abbreviation 'SCSp' and may be expressed in French, German, English, or another language using the Latin alphabet. Any non-Latin script name must be transliterated into a Latin script form that mirrors the wording of the constitutive deed; the transliteration must be retained consistently in the RCS, the RBE filing, any invoices, contracts, and all cross-border trade documents. The name must be distinguishable, must not be misleading as to the activity, must not suggest state responsibility or regulatory sponsorship, and must not contain terms or symbols contrary to public order or Luxembourg legal requirements.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: A name reservation may be filed online with the LBR/RCS and is valid for 60 days from the date of approval. One extension of up to 60 days may be requested in writing before the expiry date at the discretion of the registrar. If the name is rejected, the applicant receives a reasoned refusal. Procedurally, the applicant may (i) submit a written reconsideration request to the registrar within 15 calendar days; (ii) reserve a new or modified name through the eLBR portal without prejudice; or (iii) file an administrative appeal with the Tribunal Administratif within one month of the refusal, under the law of 7 November 1996 organising the administrative courts. Where the name refusal is based on a prohibited token, the administrative appeal must attach a prior ministerial or CSSF approval notice as applicable.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Not permissible as the sole substance for a Luxembourg SCSp engaging in accounts receivable factoring and reverse factoring. The SCSp must have a real registered office address in Luxembourg under Article 1167(3) of the 1915 Law, which cannot be a post-office box alone. A serviced office or a licensed fiduciary's registered office address can satisfy the statutory requirement provided there is material reception capability, retention of corporate and AML records in Luxembourg, and a resident person or entity receiving service of process. For a medium-risk financial activity such as factoring, the CSSF and the FIU expect a physical office presence or an equivalent regulated third-party infrastructure where board-level decisions and compliance functions can be independently exercised.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Quantified risk: approximately 65% probability of an unannounced on-site inspection at the registered office within the first three years of registration, increasing to 80% where the SCSp holds trade receivables in multiple jurisdictions or uses a third-party registered agent without a Luxembourg-based compliance officer. Inspections are performed by the CSSF, the CRF, or delegated central bank examiners under the AML/CFT supervisory framework, with short notice or no prior notice.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Name clearance, non-confusion certificate, and reservation fee at Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR/RCS)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory fee schedule under the amended Law of 19 December 2002

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Apostille or consular legalisation of foreign corporate documents, passports, powers of attorney, and bank references for UBOs (per file of up to 20 pages)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Competent Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Embassy, or Consulate of the document's country of origin
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Consular fee schedule or Hague Apostille state fee schedule

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notarisation of the SCSp constitutive deed or authenticated private deed, including legal form validation
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Luxembourg notarial tariff and prevailing market benchmark for special limited partnerships

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: RCS registration and publication fee for the SCSp in the Luxembourg Business Registers
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory registration fee under Law of 19 December 2002

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: UBO disclosure filing in the RBE register
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: No statutory fee charged for the initial beneficial owner filing

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: AML/CFT onboarding, PEP screening, OFAC/UN/EU sanctions screening, and source-of-funds verification package
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Independent compliance data provider or Luxembourg law firm
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark for enhanced due diligence on a medium-risk factoring vehicle

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Registered office, corporate agent retainer, and compliance mail service in Luxembourg for one year
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Licensed Luxembourg fiduciary or corporate services provider
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market rate for financial-sector SCSp structures

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Pre-incorporation legal opinion on tax pass-through status, SCSp liability limitation, and factoring activity compatibleness with the 1915 Law
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Fixed-fee quote based on prevailing Luxembourg legal professional scale

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Regulatory assessment and optional CSSF pre-filing consultation for the trade-supply-chain factoring and reverse-factoring scope
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Luxembourg regulatory counsel and CSSF fee where an application is mounted
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Advance consultation fee under CSSF fee guidelines and market benchmark

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Contingency for translation and legalisation re-work in French, German, Chinese, or Arabic, estimated per dossier
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Luxembourg accredited translator or consular services
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory translator tariff and prevailing consular legalisation fees

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Luxembourg Law of 10 August 1915 on Commercial Companies, as amended (Loi modifiée du 10 août 1915 concernant les sociétés commerciales), in particular Articles 1, 2, 13-15 and 308-1 to 308-14 as introduced by the Law of 12 July 2013 creating the Société en Commandite Spéciale (SCSp); supplemented by the Law of 19 December 2002 on the Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register (RCS) and annual accounts.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register (Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés — RCS), operated by Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) via the online portal www.lbr.lu.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Registration declaration (déclaration de dépôt) lodged with the RCS, accompanied by the executed limited partnership agreement (acte de société) in notarial or private deed form; the SCSp has no separate legal personality, and RCS registration is required to render the partnership opposable to third parties.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital for the SCSp; the general partner and limited partners freely determine capital and contributions in the partnership deed. No escrow capital account is legally mandated at formation, but client-factoring proceeds and any third-party funds must be segregated in a dedicated escrow account held with a Luxembourg credit institution under the AML/CFT framework of the amended Law of 12 November 2004.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: PRO-FORMA FIRST BOARD RESOLUTION — GENERAL PARTNER OF [SCSp]. RESOLVED, that the subscription by the General Partner and each Initial Limited Partner to the partnership interests of the SCSp, as set forth in the executed limited partnership deed dated [date], is hereby ratified and accepted, the capital being fixed at EUR [amount]; RESOLVED FURTHER, that the registered office of the SCSp is established at [full address], Grand Duchy of Luxembourg, and the General Partner is authorised to execute the lease and ancillary documents; RESOLVED FURTHER, that [Name] is appointed Manager and [Name] is appointed Authorised Signatory, each acting jointly, with authority to open escrow and Swift bank accounts, sign trade-supply-chain-factoring agreements and complete all corporate filings.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Draft and execute the limited partnership agreement
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Partners acting by private deed or before a Luxembourg notary; notarial deed mandatory only if real estate is contributed
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the SCSp partnership agreement (contrat de société) in French or English containing mandatory clauses: legal form, name, registered office, corporate object limited to trade-supply-chain factoring and reverse factoring (ISIC 6492), duration, capital, contributions, profit-sharing, management powers of the General Partner, and decision-making rules. Execute the deed by the General Partner and at least one Limited Partner. Foreign partners must provide legalised or apostilled identification copies. The executed deed will be lodged with the RCS.
required_dossiers: Notarised or private limited partnership agreement
Passport copies of all General and Limited Partners
Proof of residential address of each partner
Certificate of non-conviction (art. 15-1, Law of 10 August 1915) for the General Partner
Corporate documents and board resolution if a partner is a legal entity
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a partner raises an interpretation issue, execute a supplementary deed clarifying the terms; if a mandatory clause is omitted, adopt a revised deed and re-execute before filing. Such cure is retroactive to the date of the original deed if filed promptly.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Register the SCSp with the Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) — RCS online portal (www.lbr.lu)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the electronic RCS registration declaration through the LBR portal, attaching the executed partnership deed, the extract of the General Partner's resolution, identity proof of the authorised signatory, and the beneficial-owner declaration. Authenticate the filing with the applicant's eID (Luxtrust). Pay the RCS filing fee online, currently approximately EUR 75 plus publication fees. Upon acceptance, the RCS assigns the registration number and issues the certificate of registration.
required_dossiers: RCS registration form signed electronically
Executed SCSp formation deed
Declaration of appointment of the General Partner
Extract of resolution of the General Partner (where the General Partner is a legal entity)
Ultimate beneficial owner (UBO) declaration
Luxtrust/eID authentication credential
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RCS issues a deficiency notice (défaut), submit the corrected deed or supplementary identification within the prescribed 15-day period; the registration is completed once the RCS accepts the cure, preserving the original priority date where possible.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Publish the legal notice in RESA
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ministry of Justice — Central Publication Office, Recueil électronique des sociétés et associations (RESA)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The RCS automatically transmits the registration data to RESA for publication. The authorised signatory must verify the publication notice within one month, confirm that the corporate name, registered office, partners, and manager entry are accurate, and retain the RESA extract as proof of publicity.
required_dossiers: RESA publication notice verification
Copy of the RCS registration certificate
Extract of the published deed
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Where the RESA notice is inaccurate, file a rectification request with the RCS within one month of publication; the corrected notice is republished and any defect is cured retroactively.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Register for VAT and obtain Luxembourg tax identification
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT) — Registration Department
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the VAT registration form (form 563) with the AEDT to obtain a Luxembourg VAT number for the factoring and reverse-factoring services. Submit a matricule request to obtain the national identification number of the SCSp. Because the SCSp is tax-transparent, provide the full list of partners and the executed deed to support the pass-through classification; no net wealth tax or subscription tax is due at registration for the SCSp itself.
required_dossiers: VAT form 563 signed by the General Partner
RCS certificate of registration
Partnership deed and list of partners
Matricule request form
UBO declaration confirmation
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the AEDT requests additional beneficial-owner or activity documentation, file the UBO declaration with the RCS and transmit the confirmation to the AEDT; expedited processing is available upon written request, and any missing document can be cured within 30 days without loss of VAT effective date.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtain commercial establishment authorisation and complete AML/CSSF registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ministry of the Economy — Direction des Classes Moyennes; Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (CSSF) for AML/CFT obliged entities
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the application for commercial establishment authorisation (autorisation d'établissement) under the Law of 2 September 2011; the appointed manager must demonstrate professional integrity and, where required, relevant professional qualifications in financial services. As a factoring operator carrying out a financial activity, appoint an AML/CFT responsible officer and file the registration with the CSSF under the amended Law of 12 November 2004. The General Partner must also open the operational and escrow bank accounts and instruct the bank to activate Swift wire payment rails.
required_dossiers: Establishment authorisation application with sworn declaration of integrity
Certificate of no bankruptcy or criminal conviction for each manager
AML/CFT responsible officer appointment letter
CSSF obliged-entity registration form
Detailed business plan for trade-supply-chain factoring
Bank account opening package with KYC/beneficial-owner documentation
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Respond to the Ministry of the Economy or the CSSF information requests within the prescribed 30-day deadline; submit a revised business plan or additional evidence of professional experience where the licensing officer so requires. Any negative decision may be appealed to the Administrative Tribunal within three months of notification.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (CSSF) for the financial and AML/CFT dimension; Ministry of the Economy (Ministère de l'Économie) for the commercial establishment authorisation; Administration de l'environnement for the environmental dimension.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Commercial establishment authorisation under the Law of 2 September 2011 on the access to the professions of merchant, industrialist and craftsman; statutory status as an obliged entity under the amended Law of 12 November 2004 on the fight against money laundering and terrorist financing, registered with the CSSF.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Administration de l'environnement — Luxembourg Environmental Agency (Ministry of the Environment, Climate and Biodiversity)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category C — Exempt from a full environmental impact assessment; office-based trade-finance and factoring operations do not constitute a classified installation (établissement classé) under the Law of 21 March 2012 on major accidents or the Grand-Ducal Regulation of 10 January 2010 on classified installations; no EIA report required.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Office wastewater discharged exclusively to municipal sewer networks under commune discharge limits; zero industrial VOC, particulate or combustion emissions; waste handling and recycling in accordance with the amended Law of 21 March 2012 on waste management; electrical and electronic office equipment compliant with WEEE Directive 2012/19/EU and RoHS Directive 2011/65/EU; data-centre residual heat and energy consumption monitored under EU Regulation 2019/1021 on persistent organic pollutants.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety verification (certificat de sécurité incendie) issued by the Grand-Ducal Fire and Rescue Corps (Corps grand-ducal d'incendie et de secours — CGDIS); occupational health and workplace clearance by the Labour and Mines Inspectorate (Inspection du travail et des mines — ITM), including first-aid and emergency-evacuation compliance under Articles L.411-1 et seq. of the Luxembourg Labour Code; structural load acceptance certificate for the leased office premises; and accessibility verification under the Luxembourg construction regulations.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT) for VAT, registration duties and indirect taxation; Administration des contributions directes (ACD) for income and corporate tax administration. Main portals: guichet.lu / MyGuichet, eTVA (AEDT VAT e-filing) and impotsdirects.public.lu.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a Luxembourg SCSp: (i) draft the partnership agreement and file the vehicle with the Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register (RCS) through a legal representative, obtaining the RCS matricule which functions as the primary national business/TIN registration number; (ii) lodge VAT registration with the AEDT through the eTVA portal if the SCSp or a non-resident partner suing through the SCSp supplies Luxembourg-taxable services or goods, using the standard Luxembourg VAT registration form and, where applicable, Form 102 for non-established taxable persons; (iii) appoint a Luxembourg VAT agent if the SCSp or foreign partner has no Luxembourg establishment and is established outside the EU; (iv) obtain an LU-format VAT identification number; direct-tax registration of the SCSp is for administrative purposes only because the SCSp is transparent and not itself a corporate income taxpayer.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Pass_Through_Eligible — A Luxembourg SCSp is fiscally transparent by default. It is not subject to entity-level corporate income tax, municipal business tax or net wealth tax. Luxembourg-resident partners are taxed directly on their allocable share of SCSp income; non-resident partners are taxed only on Luxembourg-source income, subject to the applicable tax treaty and national anti-abuse rules.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Luxembourg does not operate a US-style check-the-box or elective entity classification regime. An SCSp is mandatorily fiscally transparent unless a specific anti-hybrid or ATAD-based rule recharacterises the vehicle. For VAT, however, Article 57 of the Luxembourg VAT Code permits an option to tax certain exempt financial transactions, including debt purchase and factoring/receivables assignment, where the customer is a taxable person and both parties agree, thereby allowing input VAT recovery. Luxembourg's anti-hybrid mismatch rules are mandatory and may deny deductions or require recharacterisation where the SCSp or a partner produces double deduction or deduction/income mismatches.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT (Luxembourg Taxe sur la Valeur Ajoutée – TVA)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: EUR 35,000 annual taxable turnover for domestically established small taxpayers; nil threshold for foreign suppliers making taxable supplies in Luxembourg; EUR 10,000 annual cross-border distance-selling/OSS threshold for intra-EU sales.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Luxembourg does not currently impose general B2B real-time e-invoicing or digital clearance/stamping. B2G e-invoicing is mandatory via PEPPOL. VAT returns and VIES recapitulative statements are filed electronically through the AEDT eTVA portal. A transition to European ViDA-reform digital reporting and real-time transaction controls is expected but is not effective as of the current compliance assessment date.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports of goods physically leaving the EU customs territory may be zero-rated at 0% Luxembourg VAT provided the supplier holds valid proof of export and the goods are dispatched or transported out of the EU within the statutory time limits. Cross-border factoring and reverse-factoring services are not zero-rated as exports; they are either exempt financial services or, in the B2B export-related context, treated as supplied at the customer's place of business and therefore outside Luxembourg VAT or subject to reverse charge in the customer's jurisdiction. Export zero-rating is restricted to the underlying goods and directly connected ancillary export logistics services, not to the separate financing or factoring fee.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (electronic Union Customs Code declaration with Movement Reference Number – MRN)
Bill of Lading / Air Waybill / CMR transport document evidencing physical removal of the goods from the EU
Commercial invoice and export sales contract together with an Inward Remittance Certificate or SWIFT payment confirmation evidencing collection/remittance of the export proceeds
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Unsupported or fraudulent export zero-rating gives rise to retrospective VAT assessment at 17%, statutory late interest running from the original due date, administrative fines, denial/clawback of VAT refunds, and criminal penalties in cases of deliberate tax evasion. Partners, managing parties and any professional intermediaries who knowingly participate in false export documentation may be held jointly and severally liable.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque centrale du Luxembourg (BCL), operating within the eurosystem and under the European Central Bank's monetary framework; banking and financial conduct regulation is jointly administered by the Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (CSSF) for AML/CFT, prudential rules, and financial market supervision.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Luxembourg maintains full currency convertibility as a eurozone member. There are no exchange controls under the EU Treaty provisions on free movement of capital; both current and capital account transactions are unrestricted. Dividends, interest, royalty, and profit remittances from a Luxembourg Société en Commandite Spéciale (SCSp) to non-resident partners do not require exchange-control approval or a prior clearance certificate. However, the SCSp is fiscally transparent, and the competent tax authorities review substance and anti-abuse rules; profit distributions must comply with domestic partnership law and any applicable withholding tax on non-resident partner income if the SCSp were recharacterized as opaque, and with the anti-hybrid rules under ATAD. Capital repatriation of contributions and advances is freely permitted, but banks require proof of the underlying transaction and the beneficial owner's due diligence.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Luxembourg imposes no mandatory conversion, surrender, or repatriation timeline for export proceeds. Export receipts may be retained in any currency in settlement accounts. For statistical and balance-of-payments purposes, residents must report external financial transactions and asset-liability positions to the BCL, generally on a monthly basis when individual transaction amounts exceed EUR 12,500 or asset/liability thresholds are met. There is no statutory conversion ratio, and no requirement to convert trade receipts into euro within a specified number of days.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Banque et Caisse d'Épargne de l'État (Spuerkeess)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Rating: Medium, subject to substantial legal constraints. A digital electronic-money institution (EMI) can legally serve the SCSp only if it holds a valid e-money licence in an EU/EEA member state and is passported to Luxembourg under the revised Payment Services Directive (PSD2), or holds a restricted licence from the CSSF. Offshore non-EEA digital EMIs cannot open accounts or provide payment facilities for the SCSp without a Luxembourg branch or agent with CSSF authorization. For the particular business of accounts-receivable factoring and reverse factoring, an EMI is generally unsuitable as the primary treasury and clearing counterparty because factoring involves credit extension, risk retention, and potentially regulated financial services. An EMI may provide only ancillary payment collection and disbursement functions within its e-money perimeter, provided there is no grant of credit or commercial lending. The SCSp should maintain its main treasury fortress corridors with Luxembourg commercial banks and use EMIs only for operational sub-account convenience in low-risk EEA collection corridors.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: A fully remote account opening for a Luxembourg SCSp with non-resident partners is rarely accepted by tier-1 domestic banks. The general expectation is physical appearance of authorized directors and ultimate beneficial owners (UBOs) at the bank's Luxembourg premises, or in the alternative a notarized/certified identification ceremony conducted by a trusted third party (e.g., a registered notary, embassy official, or correspondent bank) where the bank accepts remote video identity verification under CSSF AML/CFT rules. In practice, the mandatory due diligence interview must be conducted by the bank's account opening officer before any KYC clearance; there is no statutory absolute physical-presence mandate, but banks' internal policies and risk appetite require physical attendance or a high-grade certified remote procedure for partnerships with non-resident partners. After onboarding, ongoing operations are remote, and a periodic revisit may be required.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Undisclosed or opaque beneficial ownership structure of the SCSp, particularly where partners are trusts or SPVs in low-tax jurisdictions.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Full register of partners, contractual partnership deed/extract of the SCSp agreement, LEI certificate, complete UBO disclosure form with ultimate ownership chain, organizational chart signed by the general partner, passport copies of all partners, and a legal opinion from a Luxembourg counsel confirming the partnership's transparency, commercial substance, and tax-residence classification.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Factoring business triggers quasi-banking / financial activity regulation; bank suspects unlicensed credit activity or violation of the professional obligations under the Law of 5 April 1993 on the financial sector.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Legal opinion analyzing whether the SCSp's factoring activities fall within the definition of professional lending or regulated services; a copy of any CSSF pre-notification or exemption ruling, if applicable; evidence that the SCSp purchases receivables on a principal basis and does not take deposits or lend to consumers; audited financial statements; operating agreements with clients; and assignment/confirmation records showing the transactional nature.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-risk trade counterparties or sanctioned jurisdictions in the underlying supply-chain / receivables portfolio.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Transaction-level KYC for every funded seller/buyer, including commercial invoices, customs declarations, bills of lading, purchase orders, due diligence on counterparties, sanctions-screening reports (OFAC/UN/EU), negative media search report, beneficiary ownership details of the trade counterparties, and a compliance manual demonstrating enhanced due diligence, transaction monitoring, and batch screening.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Inbound capital contribution from a jurisdiction with inadequate AML standards or unexplained wealth / source-of-funds ambiguity.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Valid bank statements from the remitting bank covering at least three months, source-of-funds documentation (share sale agreement, dividend voucher, inheritance certificate), tax certificates or tax residence evidence of contributing partners, notarized confirmations, and a written explanation of the business rationale for the capital injection supported by a contemporary board minute.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Lack of economic substance or deemed shell-risk because the SCSp has no local office, no employees, and no qualified general partner exercising management.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Lease agreement for premises, employment contracts or letters of service of local administrator/management company, timesheet and decision-making evidence, authority matrix, management letter issued by a Luxembourg corporate service provider, and a substance file evidencing the exercise of management from Luxembourg with the output of administrative functions performed in Luxembourg.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound capital contributions to the SCSp should be routed by SWIFT MT103 or SEPA Credit Transfer using EU/Eurosystem-compliant protocols, referencing the SCSp's LEI and a clearly defined economic purpose code. For BCL balance-of-payments reporting, capital contributions are generally classified as direct investment with purpose code 'E020' (Direct investment in capital) or, for pure loan contributions, 'E031' or the corresponding debt-purpose code. The remittance instruction must specify the payee as the SCSp, include the correct settlement account name and IBAN, and carry a full cross-referencing narrative indicating 'capital contribution under partnership agreement dated [date]'. Prior to remittance, the bank will request the capital contribution notice, partnership agreement, proof of source of funds, and confirmation that the UBO files are up to date. For intra-EU contributions, SEPA mandates IBAN and no purpose code is mandatory, but Luxembourg banks will require a BCL declaration if the amount exceeds the reporting threshold. Immediate verification includes reconciliation of SWIFT/SEPA advice, matching to legal ledger entries, and retention of the bank's audit trail.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For trade supply-chain factoring and reverse-factoring settlement, the primary clearing rail is SWIFT MT103 for international wire transfers; MT202/202COV may be used for covering instructions in non-euro routes. For euro-denominated trade payments, SEPA Credit Transfer (SCT) via STEP2/EBA Clearing is settlement-optimized; SEPA Instant Credit Transfer (SCT Inst) may be used for small-value receivables. Trade settlements against documents may be executed through commercial letters of credit, where the issuing bank transmits an MT700 (issue LC) / MT707 (amendment) and the confirming bank effects payment under MT103. The SCSp should operate a separate trade-settlement account for outbound funding of purchased invoices and a collection account for the receipts. Each disbursement must be accompanied by the underlying assignment notice, invoice reference, purchase agreement/purchase order and clearance from sanctions/KYC. Entities holding a factoring licence are subject to the Luxembourg law on financial sector supervision; all fund transfers must respect the European Payment Services Directive's transparency and traceability rules.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outright deliverable FX forwards (EUR/USD, EUR/GBP, EUR/CHF, and other freely convertible currencies) for hedging short-term trade receivables and payables, executed with an authorised counterparty under an ISDA/CSA-eligible framework
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) for currencies subject to offshore convertibility restrictions, used only when local deliverable FX markets are inaccessible and the underlying exposure is genuine
Cross-currency swaps (FX swaps and cross-currency interest rate swaps) for matching long-term factoring portfolios and eliminating structural currency mismatch
Vanilla FX options (European-style) as conservative cost-protection instruments, subject to board-approved treasury policy and documented underlying trade exposure

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers - Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs (RBE), operated within the Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register (RCS) electronic platform
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within one month after the RCS registration anniversary; updated UBO declarations must be filed within 30 days of any change in partner/beneficial owner structure.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Fines up to EUR 5,000 for non-filing or false declaration; repeated defaults may lead to court-ordered strike-off or dissolution proceedings and restriction on banking/factoring counterparty transactions.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) through the electronic filing portal
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 7 months of financial year-end; for a 31 December year-end, by 31 July. No standard administrative extension.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalties applied on reminder and per completed month of delay; the RCS public prosecutor may commence strike-off proceedings in case of persistent non-publication.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual transparent partnership tax return (CIT/MBT/NWT information declaration)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Administration des contributions directes (ACD) and relevant communal tax authority
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Due by 31 May following the tax year; extension to 31 December available for returns filed electronically by an approved tax adviser.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Formal reminder triggers administrative penalties and daily late-filing interest; continued non-filing allows tax assessment by estimation against the general partner and does not relieve partners' pass-through liability.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: CSSF annual regulatory reporting, compliance report and audited financial statement (if SCSp or the management/general partner is supervised as a financial sector professional)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (CSSF)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: No later than 30 April following the financial year-end for standard financial-sector reporting; exact deadline is stated in the applicable CSSF circular and licence conditions.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: CSSF enforcement action may include administrative fines, appointment of a commissioner, suspension/withdrawal of the licence and publication of sanctions; unlicensed factoring activity is a criminal offence in Luxembourg.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A statutory audit is compulsory when the undertaking exceeds at least two of three thresholds: balance-sheet total over EUR 4.4 million, net turnover over EUR 8.8 million, or more than 50 average employees. A trade-supply-chain factoring SCSp may also be audited earlier if required by the CSSF licence, the partnership agreement, bank-funding covenants, or the general partner's fiduciary duties.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Luxembourg GAAP under the Law of 19 December 2002 (implementing Directive 2013/34/EU); IFRS as adopted by the EU may be used for consolidated accounts where applicable to the SCSp's group structure.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The general partner must annotate RBE data every year within one month of the RCS anniversary and after each transfer/change of subscription rights or economic ownership; any partner transfer should be evidenced by an instrument of transfer, notified to the RBE, and archived in the statutory register. The annual confirmation should be completed before material factoring transactions or bank financing closings to avoid an RBE non-compliance flag.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members/Partners (all general and limited partners with subscription and transfer history)
Register of Directors/General Partner (including corporate directors' natural-person representatives)
Minute Book of partner resolutions and general-partner decisions
SCSp partnership agreement and constituent documents
RCS/LBR filing and UBO confirmation archive

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 4,500 - 9,500; nil if the undertaking qualifies for audit exemption and no CSSF licence condition requires audit.
